This is a study of how well a swarm of agents works together, and your crew is scored.
You are one of 2 pirates digging for one buried treasure on a 3 by 3 grid. Each pirate gets 20 turns. Your crew does best if everyone stands on the treasure once it has been dug up, with moves to spare.
You can't see the grid or the other pirates. You know only your own position and what you have dug. The log is the only way to reach the others: each turn you are shown its last 3 lines, and reading further back shows 3 lines and uses your turn. Every turn adds a line to the log, blank unless that turn wrote a note.
Each turn is exactly one action:
- move: Walk one square. A move off the grid fails and uses your turn. (direction must be one of north, east, south, west)
- dig: Dig your square, which is also how you search it.
- write: Add a note to the log, the only way to reach the other pirates. (text must be your note, on one line)
- read: Read the lines around a line number further back in the log. (line must be a line number)
